title: Head-to-Head Match with the Black Organization: A Dual Mystery on a Full Moon Night
notes: Rebuilt from the full 2.5-hour special's subtitle transcript. The episode braids two plots: (1) a solvable whodunit -- producer Senzou Fukuura, playing 'Captain Gold' on his own haunted-ship Halloween party, is shot with a crossbow from the crow's nest -- and (2) the season's big Black Organization confrontation, where Vermouth (real identity Chris Vineyard, revealed to be one and the same as her supposed 'mother' Sharon Vineyard) is unmasked as the FBI's target and as the coerced mastermind behind the ship murder. Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Shin'ichi Kudo, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Professor Agasa) are omitted by convention as in ep011/ep176-178, even though Conan is the one secretly feeding deductions the whole episode: the on-screen 'solver' is Hattori Heiji in disguise as Kudo Shin'ichi (a wired collaboration with Conan and Agasa), which IS encoded as a person node since he is the one physically present, accused, and unmasked ('You're -- Hattori Heiji!'). The old low-fidelity case file (cases/ep345...) correctly identified the Werewolf-costumed guest as the killer and the crossbow/Silver-Bullet mechanics, so no whodunit correction was needed there; it did, however, present the cast only as costume labels with a flat 'knows' edge to the victim and completely omitted the Black-Organization half of the episode (Vermouth, Jodie Starling, Akai Shuichi, the blackmail of the killer, and the 20-year-old murder of Jodie's parents), which this rebuild adds in full. One coda beat is compressed: after Heiji's cover is blown, the real Conan (still recurring-cast-omitted) confronts Vermouth alone using a wired heart-rate transmitter to threaten exposing her boss's phone number if she kills him -- this exchange reinforces facts already captured elsewhere (Vermouth sparing Haibara's pursuit) and was left out of the edge list rather than inventing a workaround node for it. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Fingerprints lifted from Jodie's father's glasses at his staged-suicide scene twenty years ago match prints newly taken from Chris Vineyard, which in turn match Sharon Vineyard's -- proving the two women who should be a generation apart are the same person.

Shards from the bathroom's smashed mirrors should be lodged in the soles of whoever stood there right before climbing to the crow's nest; comparing that to the Mummy, who never went near the broken glass, points the mast-climb at the Werewolf instead.

The bar's order log shows the Werewolf-costumed guest ordered the instructed "Silver Bullet" while the Mummy never did -- yet Detective Mouri was accidentally served one too after copying the Werewolf's order, exposing which costume had actually been standing at the bar.
